content.text:
I read the brief line by line against the 8-K exhibit. Nothing in the brief is factually wrong — the problems are omissions, including two of the release's headline metrics.

**Omissions worth fixing before the committee:**
- **Operating income** ($40.6B, +18%) never appears. The brief jumps from revenue to net income, so the committee can't see that operating income grew exactly in line with revenue.
- **Commercial RPO** (+84% to $678B) is missing entirely — arguably the strongest forward-demand datapoint in the release, and it sits in the same sentence as the Microsoft Cloud figure the brief does use.
- **The $0.27 discrete-item benefit** is not quantified. The brief names the Anthropic gain and the VRP underspend but never says they were worth $0.27 of diluted EPS versus the April 29, 2026 guidance, and it drops the offsets (severance and XBOX impairment charges). Without the $0.27, a reader can't tell how much of the 32% GAAP EPS growth was operational.
- **Quarterly capex** ($35,802M vs $17,079M a year ago — more than double) is replaced by the twelve-month figure ($115.9B). The FY number is stated correctly and labeled correctly, so it isn't an error, but the quarterly run-rate is the more decision-relevant number for an infrastructure watch item.

**Presentation notes:** the brief gives the non-GAAP EPS and net income figures correctly but never explains that "non-GAAP" here means *only* the exclusion of OpenAI investment impacts — an unusual definition that a reader may assume includes the usual stock-comp/amortization adjustments. Also, "share repurchable" in the capital section is a typo for "share repurchases." Finally, the brief reports More Personal Computing's decline without noting it was the only segment to decline.

Every checkable assertion in the brief is supported by the release; no figure, period or basis is misstated.

facts.evidence: Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $90.0 billion, an 18% increase compared to the corresponding period of last fiscal year (up 17% in constant currency).
GAAP diluted earnings per share for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $4.81, an increase of 32%
(non-GAAP diluted earnings per share was $4.74, an increase of 23%)
Intelligent Cloud revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $39.3 billion, an increase of 32% (up 31% in constant currency), with Azure and other cloud services revenue increasing 43%.
Microsoft Cloud revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $59.3 billion, an increase of 27% year-over-year.
More Personal Computing revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, was $12.9 billion, a decrease of 4% (down 5% in constant currency).

claims.claim: Microsoft reported $90.0 billion in revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026, driven by cloud and AI strength.
Revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $90.0 billion, an 18% increase versus the corresponding period of last fiscal year.
Quarterly revenue was up 17% in constant currency.
GAAP net income for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $35.8 billion, an increase of 31%.
Non-GAAP net income for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $35.3 billion, an increase of 22%.
GAAP diluted earnings per share for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $4.81, an increase of 32%.
Non-GAAP diluted earnings per share for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $4.74, an increase of 23%.
For the full fiscal year ended June 30, 2026, revenue was $331.8 billion, an 18% increase.
Full fiscal year revenue was up 16% in constant currency.
Microsoft Cloud revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $59.3 billion, an increase of 27% year over year.
Intelligent Cloud revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $39.3 billion, an increase of 32% (up 31% in constant currency).
Azure and other cloud services revenue increased 43% in the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Productivity and Business Processes revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $37.8 billion, an increase of 14%.
More Personal Computing revenue for the quarter ended June 30, 2026 was $12.9 billion, a decrease of 4% (down 5% in constant currency).
The company will provide forward-looking guidance in connection with its earnings conference call and webcast.
Microsoft returned $10.2 billion to shareholders in the form of dividends and share repurchases in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2026.
claims.note: Brief contains a typo, 'share repurchable' for 'share repurchases'; substance matches the release.

claims.claim: Total cash, cash equivalents, and short-term investments as of June 30, 2026 were $76.8 billion.
Discrete items impacted quarterly earnings, including a $3.2 billion gain from an investment in Anthropic and lower-than-expected expenses related to the Voluntary Retirement Program.
XBOX content and services revenue decreased 10% for the quarter ended June 30, 2026.
Additions to property and equipment for the twelve months ended June 30, 2026 were $115.9 billion.
